sentences.text: This crocodile was small, growing to a length between two and two-and-a-half meters.
Its skull features a unique horn-like projection on the squamosal bone that points outward.
Five teeth were located in the front of the upper jaw, with the rear four arranged in a straight row.
A sharp, thin spike extended from the main body of the forehead bone.
Fossil evidence reveals a direct predator-prey link between this crocodile and the giant Aldabra tortoise.
Unhealed puncture wounds on the tortoise's shell and hip bone prove a violent attack occurred.
Scientists first uncovered these remains in Quaternary layers at Point Hodoul on the Seychelles atoll.
The genus was formally named and described by researcher Brochu in the year 2006.
Experts hypothesize the animal attacked giant tortoises head-on at water sources to reach the neck shield.
Genetic analysis places this species within the family Crocodylidae.
It inhabited Aldabra Atoll during the Pleistocene epoch.
The species existed from 0.129 to 0.0117 million years ago.
It remains debated whether this crocodile is a close relative of Voay or Crocodylus palaeindicus.
Researchers also suggest its small size and that of Osteolaemus may have evolved independently.
